BiblicalUsage: Poreketh is the veil, the sacred screen that hung before the most holy place. Exodus describes it in blue and purple and scarlet, worked with cherubim, and Leviticus warns Aaron not to come at all times within the veil before the mercy seat. Numbers gives the priests charge of everything within the veil, and Chronicles shows the same veil in Solomon's temple.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the veil taught Israel the weight of holiness: God was near, but not to be approached carelessly. And I hold that Christ's death tore that veil, so the way into the holiest is open now to all who come by him.
